pr_title: Maintain selection on file/dir deletion in project panel
pr_body:
Closes #20444

- Focus on next file/dir on deletion.
- Focus on prev file/dir in case where it's last item in worktree.
- Tested when multiple files/dirs are being deleted.

Release Notes:

- Maintain selection on file/dir deletion in project panel.
pr_comments:
@SomeoneToIgnore upon writing test cases i realised what i did earlier, i.e. focusing on just next entry (idx + 1), is straight up wrong as say on deleting dir,  it might choose it's child as `next_selection`.

For this to work,  `find_next_selection` fun, should be tree-aware. I updated the logic (trying to mimick functionality of how VSCode does it and what feels sensible).

Now, it chooses bottom-most marked entry which does not have any marked ancestor. And, select it's sibling.

Handled below test cases:
1. middle file removed from directory
2. last file removed from directory
3. root level file removed
4. nested dir + parent dir removed together
5. mixed selection removed (subdir file + parent file + root file)
6. all contents removed (all root dirs + all root files)
7. nested selection removed (parent dir + subdir + file inside subdir)

Note: I had to supress error `no such entry` on delete file (if file does not exists), as it used to panic that thread, and below logic for `next_selection`  wouldn't run. This panic often happens when say you have list like `dir1` and `dir1/a.rs`, so after deleting `dir1` , `a.rs` won't be there.

Updated to a sanitization approach and added tests for multiple worktrees.

I also had to update the `compare_paths` function in `paths.rs` to handle cases where file names are the same, but the extensions differ. Previously, this compare func completely ignored the presence of extensions when sorting, leading to unpredictable sorting of such files. Since we use stable sorting everywhere, the original order of those files was retained.

This was problematic when choosing the last marked element. If multiple files with the same name were marked in the directory, it could end up selecting the wrong one than what's in `visible_entries`.

Let me know your thoughts on this. I also added a test case for this change, and all existing cases passed.
Let me know if you spot any other nitpicks or performance stuff. I tried to avoid those issues you mentioned in this one.

issue_context.title: Wrong element focused when deleting items in project panel
issue_context.body:
### Check for existing issues

- [X] Completed

### Describe the bug / provide steps to reproduce it

After removing a file/folder from sidebar, keyboard focus is switched to the first entry in the panel. This makes deleting multiple files very impractical.

Solution would be to focus the next file after the deleted one.


### Environment

Zed: v0.160.7 (Zed)
OS: Linux X11 arch unknown
Memory: 62.5 GiB
Architecture: x86_64
GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 2060 with Max-Q Design || NVIDIA || 565.57.01

### If applicable, add mockups / screenshots to help explain present your vision of the feature

_No response_

review_comments:
Can we remove a worktree root?
Not insisting to fix that if we cannot, but curious if there's an easy test to add just after this.
Or maybe even delete both roots? Maybe even with marked files in them?

I tried this, but there seems to be an issue with the existing deletion logic when the root is selected or marked.

E.g.
```
> root1
   > some.txt
> root2
```

Case 1: If you select `some.txt` first and then mark `root2`, it will prompt for the deletion of `some.txt`, which is expected.

Case 2: If you select `root2` first and then mark `some.txt`, it will not prompt for anything. It should prompt for `some.txt`.

I'm considering fixing this in another PR, as it might require changes to either the `marked_entries` function (which is being used at lot places) or the logic for marking/selecting the root. I haven’t fully dug into this yet.

What do you think?
Yeah, we're quite stuck here anyway, so let's not touch the roots yet, thank you for considering this.

Let's, before every change selection (initial state like here, selection changed after some deletion assert, etc.), assert the way how the tree looked with the selection.
So, there's always "selection before" vs. "selection after" comparison, which makes these tests more readable.

For the tests below too.

Overall, sounds somewhat heavy as we're iterating over all `entries` in the project panel.
That might be thousands of files easily.

Can we be smarter?
We have a `marked_entries()` method that will return all entries that will be deleted.

We could get all their entries in ~O(1) each and 
1. Do the sanitization I've been talking about before, removing all entries that are subfiles/subdirs (this subset can be determined way above this, in the removal method)
2. Then, we can start looking for entries that are adjacent to the last removed entry: presumably, we can find a parent dir, and then reverse-iterate this subset only, finding the new selection target.
